subject: storytime
title: The North Wind and the Sun
about: Aesop's fable of the bragging North Wind and the Sun, who have a contest to see which of them can get a man's coat off: the harder the Wind blows, the tighter the man holds on, but the Sun's gentle warmth does it easily. It gives first graders a clear lesson about being gentle instead of rough, and it is easy to act out. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Act it out with a jacket: blow hard while he holds it tight, then be the warm sun and see what he does.

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Who can get the coat off, the strong wind or the warm sun?

passage.text:
The North Wind liked to brag.
"I am stronger than you," he said to the Sun.
"Let's find out," said the Sun.
Down below, a man walked on a path.
He had on a big, warm coat.
"Who can get his coat off?" asked the Sun.
"That is easy!" said the Wind.
"I will go first."
***
The Wind blew.
Whoosh!
The man held on to his coat.
The Wind blew harder.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
The man held his coat tight.
The Wind blew as hard as he could.
Leaves flew off the trees.
But the man held his coat tighter and tighter.
At last the Wind gave up.
***
Then it was the Sun's turn.
The Sun did not blow.
The Sun just smiled and shone.
The man felt warm.
He let go of his coat.
The Sun shone some more.
"It is so hot!" said the man.
He took off his coat.
He sat down in the shade to rest.
***
The Sun had won!
The Wind's mouth fell open.
"How did you do that?" he asked.
"I did not blow or push," said the Sun.
"I was just gentle and warm."
"Then the man took off his coat by himself."
The Wind did not brag after that.
Gentle and kind works better than rough and strong.

cards.q: Who said, 'I am stronger than you'?
cards.note: The North Wind is the cold wind that blows down from the north in winter.

cards.q: What did the Wind and the Sun want the man to take off?
cards.note: The coat is the whole contest: whoever gets it off wins.

cards.q: What did the man do when the Wind blew?
cards.note: The harder the wind blew, the tighter he held on, so the Wind only made things worse.

cards.q: What did the Sun do to win?
cards.note: The warm sunshine made the man so hot that he took the coat off by himself.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The bragging starts it all, before the contest even begins.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The man took his coat off for the Sun, so the Sun won and the Wind stopped bragging.

cards.q: How did the Wind feel when the man took off his coat?
cards.note: His mouth fell open, so ask him to make the surprised face the Wind made.
Pushing hard only made the man hold on tighter, but being gentle got the job done.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'brag' mean?
cards.note: To brag is to tell everyone how great you are, the way the Wind did at the start.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
